source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Use room number plus the client's statement because location can serve as a person-specific identifier when a wristband is unclear.","B":"Use a family member's recognition because relative confirmation can replace the organization's required identification process.","C":"Use two acceptable person-specific identifiers according to policy and address the unreadable wristband through the facility process.","D":"Use only the client's stated name because a second person-specific identifier is unnecessary when the client is alert."}}
source_row.rationale: Joint Commission guidance requires reliable person-specific identification and does not accept room number as an identifier. Option C is correct because it uses two acceptable identifiers and follows the facility process for an unreadable band. Option A incorrectly uses room number, Option B substitutes family recognition for the identification process, and Option D uses only one identifier.
source_row.source_detail: The Joint Commission — Two Patient Identifiers: Understanding the Requirements, FAQ updated 2026-04-21: acceptable identifiers are person-specific (for example name, date of birth, assigned identification number, telephone number); room number or physical location is not acceptable; organizations define their approved process. Joint Commission standards FAQ last updated 2026-04-21; current requirements live-rechecked 2026-08-15. NCSBN first-check: Client Needs — Safe and Effective Care Environment — Safety and Infection Prevention and Control: patient identification, specimen collection, asepsis, high-alert medication safeguards, fall prevention and communication that prevents safety events as applicable. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.
